bluetooth_classic.notes: ble_role is secondary_control on the strength of SoundcoreManager, which sends these frames over GATT to the A3951, A3027, A3028, A3029 and A3935 (reported). For the A3947 and A3116 BLE is only known to be used for discovery. The vendor Android app uses BLE only to find devices and, on party speakers, for speaker linking. This spec declares no GATT service. address_shared_with_ble is false as confirmed on the A3947: its advertisement came from a random resolvable address and carried the public BR/EDR address in its manufacturer data. The older vendor app also stores the two addresses separately. wake_required is false: earbuds power on when taken out of or opened in the case, and headphones and speakers from their power button, which is ordinary power-on rather than a wake gesture.

profiles.notes: SDP service name "Spp1", profile descriptor SPP 1.2. Every soundcore frame in the A3947 capture travels on this channel. Channel 15 is what that unit's SDP record said; resolve it by UUID. Secure false: the vendor Android app opens every control socket with the insecure constructor (static analysis), on a link that is already bonded for audio.

SDP service name "CSR GAIA" with an SPP profile descriptor. Every soundcore frame in the Motion+ capture travels on this channel. The browse showed no record with the SPP service class 00001101-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, so a client that asks SDP for SPP finds nothing. OpenSCQ30 pins this UUID for the A3116, and its changelog records repeated fixes for Motion+ connection problems.

The vendor app's model table gives SPP, not a vendor UUID, for the Life Q30, Life Tune and Life Q35, the Liberty 2 family, Liberty Air 2 and Air 2 Pro, Life A2 NC and Life Dot 2 NC. The channel was not observed.

SDP service name "TOTA", Bestechnic's test-over-the-air service. NOT the soundcore control channel, although it carries the SPP class. A client that opens "SPP by UUID" on an A3947 lands here and gets no answer to 08 ee frames. Its protocol is not documented here.

SDP service name "BESOTA": the Bestechnic firmware-update channel. The vendor app bundles a BES updater that opens an insecure RFCOMM socket to this UUID (static analysis). Firmware transfer is out of scope; see features.

SDP service name "RFCOMM COM". This UUID is Google Fast Pair's Message Stream, which the Android system (not the soundcore app) opens. In the capture it carried the Fast Pair model ID of the Liberty 4 NC, D1E4E3, a battery report for left, right and case, the device's BLE address, and the phone's platform message. It is a public Google protocol and a read-only source of battery data; see helpful_urls.
Audio Sink, AVDTP on L2CAP PSM 25, in both captured SDP records.
Controller and Target records, AVCTP on PSM 23, in both captures.
Hands-Free unit: RFCOMM channel 3 on the A3947, channel 12 on the A3116, in the captures.
Headset: RFCOMM channel 1 on the A3947, channel 11 on the A3116, in the captures.

framing.notes:
Frame: five direction bytes (08 ee 00 00 00 phone to device, 09 ff 00 00 01 device to phone), two command bytes, a u16 little-endian length at offset 7 that counts the WHOLE frame from the first direction byte to the last byte, the payload, then (on most models) one checksum byte. Split the stream by the length field alone, which works whether or not a checksum is present.
Checksum is "other" only because it is per model. On models that have it (A3947 and A3028/A3029 here, and every model OpenSCQ30 supports except the A3116) it is sum8 over every preceding byte of the frame, starting with the first direction byte, i.e. `auto: checksum` with checksum_start 0. Example, confirmed on the A3947: 08 ee 00 00 00 01 01 0a 00 sums to 0x102, so the checksum is 02. The A3116 appends none: its state request is 08 ee 00 00 00 01 01 09 00 and every reply's length field equals header plus payload. A client that must support unknown models can tell the two apart from the first reply: recompute the sum over all but the last byte and compare. OpenSCQ30 instead fixes it per model (ChecksumKind in lib/src/devices/soundcore/common/packet.rs).
On a sync loss, scan to the next 09 ff 00 00 01 and read its length.

serial.notes: Correlation: a reply's bytes 5-6 repeat the command it answers, and an acknowledgement is that frame with an empty payload. OpenSCQ30 matches replies to requests by those two bytes. max_in_flight 1 is what the captures show: the vendor app sent each frame only after the previous one was answered. read_chunk_bytes is the vendor app's read buffer (static analysis). The app's generic serial link waits 50 or 500 ms after a reply before sending the next queued frame. The captured sessions show 20-100 ms gaps, so the delay depends on the model's manager and is not stated as a requirement.

methods.notes: The name the A3947 gave to a remote-name request in the capture was "soundcore Liberty 4 NC" (lower-case brand, the current styling). Older products say "Soundcore ..." (the Motion+ manual's own spelling). Anker's conference speakers ("Anker PowerConf") appear in the vendor app's model table but match neither needle; their command set is not documented here. Earbuds and headphones answer an inquiry only while in pairing mode (device.pairing.enter_pairing_mode). Most users will already have the device bonded to the host, in which case a client lists bonded devices instead of running an inquiry, which is what both open-source clients do.

The Liberty 4 NC (A3947) as seen in the SoundcoreManager #162 capture, advertising from a random resolvable address before the phone connected. Its advertisement carried three AD structures. The first is Google Fast Pair service data (0xfe2c), which holds per-user account-key data and is not reproduced here. The second is a 32-bit service UUID list, 01 4e f5 da. The third is manufacturer-specific data (AD type 0xff) of eight bytes: the device's PUBLIC BR/EDR address, most significant byte first, then 00 00. Those bytes do NOT start with a Bluetooth SIG company ID; a parser that reads the first two as one gets a meaningless 0xeee8. A client scans, reads the BR/EDR address out of the manufacturer data, and opens RFCOMM to THAT address, not the advertiser's. For an unknown unit aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff the structure is 09 ff aa bb cc dd ee ff 00 00.

What an older vendor app build (2.9.9, which predates the Liberty 4 NC) looks for: a complete 128-bit service UUID list whose one entry is the model's code (010af5da-... for the Motion+, 0112f5da-... for the Life Q30/Tune and most earbuds; protocol_details.model_table has the rest). Next to it, manufacturer data of seven bytes whose first six are the BR/EDR address LEAST significant byte first (the opposite order to the A3947 above). The app keeps the BLE address separately and connects RFCOMM to the address from the manufacturer data. Not seen on air: the Motion+ capture contains no advertisement from the speaker.

host_compatibility.basis: Both captures are Android HCI snoop logs of the vendor app driving a device over RFCOMM: an A3947 on the vendor UUID record (channel 15) and an A3116 on its vendor UUID record (channel 1).
OpenSCQ30's Linux backend opens the same RFCOMM service through BlueZ (lib/src/connection_backend/linux/rfcomm.rs), selecting the vendor UUID from the SDP record. Not run by this project.
OpenSCQ30 ships a Windows RFCOMM backend (lib/src/connection_backend/windows/rfcomm.rs). SoundcoreManager reaches its supported models from Windows over BLE GATT instead. Not run by this project.
CoreBluetooth has no RFCOMM API, and the control channel this spec documents is RFCOMM. No MFi (iAP2) record appears in either captured SDP browse.
host_compatibility.notes: The vendor ships an iOS app, so iPhones reach these devices somehow, most plausibly over the BLE GATT path SoundcoreManager uses; see the `ble` verdict below. macOS is outside this verdict: IOBluetooth exposes RFCOMM.

host_compatibility.basis: SoundcoreManager drives the A3951, A3027, A3028, A3029 and A3935 over a GATT service that carries the same 08 ee / 09 ff frames (soundcore-lib/src/ble/btleplug/connection.rs), so for those models a CoreBluetooth client can probably do the same. Whether the A3947 and A3116 expose such a service is unknown, and the iOS app was not examined.

mac_prefixes.notes: Seen as the public BR/EDR address of the Liberty 4 NC (A3947) in the SoundcoreManager #162 capture. IEEE assigns it to Fantasia Trading LLC, Anker's US trading company. One unit only. The BLE advertisement of the same unit used a random resolvable address, so this prefix matches only the Classic address.
Seen as the BR/EDR address of the Motion+ (A3116) in the OpenSCQ30 #215 capture. IEEE assigns it to Fihonest Communication Co., Ltd, not to Anker. One unit only.

identification.notes: The BLE service UUIDs are model codes, not GATT services a client can open. daf54e01-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb is what the Liberty 4 NC advertises, as a 32-bit UUID (AD type 0x05, raw bytes 01 4e f5 da), seen in the capture (confirmed). The other two are the vendor app's expected codes for the Motion+ and for the Life Q30/Tune (and most other earbuds): 128-bit, AD type 0x07, raw little-endian bytes fb 34 9b 5f 80 00 00 80 00 10 00 00 da f5 <code> 01 (reported, not seen on air). The two encodings put the four significant bytes in opposite order. The whole per-SKU list is protocol_details.model_table. The Classic inquiry name is in the bt_classic_inquiry method: the A3947 answered "soundcore Liberty 4 NC". Older models use "Soundcore <name>" (the Motion+ manual says "Soundcore Motion+").

device.name: Anker soundcore Earbuds, Headphones and Speakers
device.notes:
Anker's soundcore range covers true-wireless earbuds (Liberty, Life, Space), over-ear headphones (Life Q, Space Q) and portable speakers (Motion, and others). The "soundcore" app adjusts the settings the hardware keeps itself: ambient-sound mode (noise cancelling, transparency, normal), equaliser, button mapping, volume limits, auto power-off and firmware. Audio itself is plain A2DP/HFP and needs no app. Everything in this spec is optional to using the product. The spec exists so the settings stay reachable without the vendor app, which now asks for an account and shows advertising and an AI assistant (see evidence.open_questions).
TRANSPORT. The app talks to the device over an RFCOMM (Serial Port style) socket, opened insecure (no bond needed for the socket itself), to a per-model service UUID. On most models (every speaker and most earbuds in the vendor app's table) that is a VENDOR UUID, 0cf12d31-fac3-4553-bd80-d6832e7b followed by the four digits of the SKU (A3947 -> 0cf12d31-fac3-4553-bd80-d6832e7b3947). Older earbuds and headphones (Liberty 2 family, Liberty Air 2 / Air 2 Pro, Life Q30/Q35/Tune, Life A2 NC, Life Dot 2 NC) use the standard SPP UUID 00001101-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb instead. Open the vendor UUID when the SDP record has one: on the A3947 the SPP class belongs to a different, chip-vendor service (see bluetooth_classic.profiles). The Motion+ publishes no SPP-class record at all.
FRAMES. Phone to device: 08 ee 00 00 00, a two-byte command, a u16 little-endian length counting the WHOLE frame, the payload, and on most models a checksum byte (sum of every preceding byte, mod 256). Device to phone: 09 ff 00 00 01 and the same layout. A reply echoes the command bytes. A set is acknowledged with an empty-payload frame carrying the same command. The Motion+ (A3116) sends and expects NO checksum byte, so its length field counts header + payload only (a bare request is 9 bytes, not 10). OpenSCQ30 treats this as a per-model setting and the A3116 is the only model it knows of without the checksum. See bluetooth_classic.serial.framing and protocol_details.frame_grammar.
MODELS. The protocol is a FAMILY keyed by SKU, not one command set. Command IDs overlap with different meanings: 01 81 is volume on the Motion+ and auto play/pause on earbuds; 01 83 is auto power-off on the Motion+ and touch tones on earbuds. The state reply (01 01) has a different layout on every model. This spec declares four variants with full detail: A3947 and A3116 (captured) and A3028/A3029 (reported). The SKU-to-UUID table for 60-odd more is protocol_details.model_table. For any model not declared here, take its command set from OpenSCQ30's per-model module (lib/src/devices/soundcore/<sku>.rs) before sending anything.
BLE. Many models also advertise over BLE, and the vendor app can find a device that way: the advertisement carries a model-coded service UUID and the device's BR/EDR address in its manufacturer data, and the app then opens RFCOMM to that address. On some models a GATT service tunnels the same frames. SoundcoreManager drives the A3951, A3027, A3028, A3029 and A3935 that way, which is presumably how the iOS app reaches them. That GATT layout is out of scope here (remaining_unknowns).
OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately: firmware transfer (OTA over BES, Qualcomm GAIA or per-model updaters; only its existence is recorded, under features), party-mode speaker linking, the charging-case display and recording on newer cases, HearID hearing-profile upload, the Anka AI and translation features, and the Anker account cloud. Anker SOLIX power stations and eufy cameras use unrelated protocols and are not covered.

openness.notes: Anker publishes nothing about the protocol. Two independent open-source clients implement it: OpenSCQ30 (Rust; Linux, Windows and Android, over RFCOMM) and SoundcoreManager (Rust/Tauri; Windows, over BLE GATT). Both were used as sources here and are cited by file. Neither is affiliated with Anker.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: Earbuds enter pairing mode on their own the first time the case is opened. Headphones and speakers enter it from a power or Bluetooth button. Outside pairing mode the device reconnects to known hosts and answers no inquiry.

steps.expect: The Bluetooth indicator fades blue in and out.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the vendor app (or turn its phone's Bluetooth off) before connecting from another client: both captures show the app holding the control channel for the whole session, and whether the device takes a second control connection is unknown. If the device will not appear, remove it from the host's Bluetooth list and pair again, as the Motion+ manual advises.

pairing.notes: This is a Bluetooth audio device, and it bonds for A2DP/HFP like any headset. Both open-source clients list only BONDED devices, so bonding is in practice required. The CONTROL socket, however, is opened insecure by the vendor Android app (bluetooth_classic.profiles[].secure: false), which is normal for a headset. Just Works is inferred from the hardware having no display or keypad; both captures begin with an existing bond, so the pairing exchange was not seen.

unpair.notes: No button, command or app action is known that removes one host from the device's own pairing list. Removing the device on the host side (forget it in Bluetooth settings) is always possible. The factory reset presumably clears the device side, but the manuals do not say so.

credentials.notes: No application-layer key and no login. The control socket needs no authentication beyond what the Bluetooth link already has. Whether newer models add an app-layer handshake is not known. Neither capture shows one, and OpenSCQ30 sends none (remaining_unknowns).
stored_on_device: Bluetooth link keys for each paired host (the standard BR/EDR bond)

factory_reset.effect: Returns the earbuds or headphones to their shipped state. The manuals do not list what is cleared. On Bluetooth audio products this usually means the paired-device list and app settings (EQ, controls), but that is not established here.

methods.description: Put the device in pairing mode, pair it as an audio device from the phone or computer, then open an insecure RFCOMM socket to the model's control UUID and send the state request.
methods.name: Pair from the host's Bluetooth settings, then open the control socket

steps.action: Put the device into pairing mode (see device.pairing.enter_pairing_mode for each model).
steps.expect: The pairing indicator flashes (white on A3947 case LEDs; blue on the A3028/A3029 and A3116).

steps.action: Select the device in the host's Bluetooth settings and accept the pairing.
steps.expect: The host bonds and connects A2DP/HFP.
steps.notes: Secure Simple Pairing with no PIN is expected for hardware with no display or keypad; not observed in either capture.

steps.action: Browse SDP and pick the control record: the vendor UUID 0cf12d31-fac3-4553-bd80-d6832e7b<sku> if present, otherwise 00001101-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb.
steps.notes: OpenSCQ30's default rule (lib/src/devices/soundcore/common/device.rs): any UUID matching 0cf12d31-fac3-4553-bd80-d6832e7 in its first 108 bits wins, SPP is the fallback. On an A3947 the SPP record is the wrong one (BES test service, channel 12).

steps.action: Open an insecure RFCOMM socket to that UUID.
steps.expect: Channel 15 on the A3947 and channel 1 on the A3116 in the captures; resolve by SDP rather than hard-coding.

steps.action: Send the model's state request (a3947_request_state, a3116_request_state or a3028_request_state) and parse the reply.
steps.expect: A 09 ff 00 00 01 01 01 frame. Its length field says how many bytes to read.

setup.notes: The only setup is ordinary Bluetooth pairing from the host's own Bluetooth settings, the same step every manual gives. The vendor app does not provision anything. It lists already-bonded devices, recognises the model from the SDP record or the name, and opens the control socket. Its account sign-up is for the vendor cloud, which the device never talks to. Confidence is medium: the steps come from the FCC-filed manuals, and the capture sessions started with the devices already bonded, so the pairing itself was not observed.

rejoin.notes: A new phone pairs like any other host: enter pairing mode and pair. The A3947 and A3028/A3029 remember more than one host (dual connection), and the A3116 reconnects to the last host at power-on and re-enters pairing mode on its Bluetooth button. Nothing in the control protocol is tied to a host or an account.

testing.notes: Nobody in this project has driven a soundcore device from this document. It was checked against two public Android HCI snoop logs of the vendor app. The first is a Liberty 4 NC (A3947), attached to https://github.com/gmallios/SoundcoreManager/issues/162: 7 frames each way on the vendor RFCOMM channel (state request, LDAC query, five sound-mode sets and their acknowledgements). The second is a Motion+ (A3116), attached to https://github.com/Oppzippy/OpenSCQ30/issues/215: 22 frames to the speaker and 31 back (state, voice prompt, a 05 01 query, seven EQ presets, custom EQ, volume and auto-power-off). The checksum on every A3947 frame was recomputed. So were the length field and the absent checksum on every A3116 frame, the SDP records of both units, and the A3947's BLE advertisement. Those facts are marked `confirmed`. Everything else is `reported`.

variants.notes: soundcore Liberty 4 NC, true-wireless earbuds with adaptive ANC, LDAC and a charging case with a button. FCC ID 2AOKB-A3947. Control on the vendor RFCOMM record 0cf12d31-fac3-4553-bd80-d6832e7b3947 ("Spp1", channel 15 in the capture). Frames carry the checksum. SoC family: Bestechnic (BES), going by the SDP records "TOTA" and "BESOTA" (BES test and OTA services). Captured firmware 04.88 on both buds. OpenSCQ30 module: lib/src/devices/soundcore/a3947.rs.

Soundcore Motion+, a 30 W portable speaker (Bluetooth 5.0, aptX, AUX in, True Wireless Stereo pairing with a second Motion+). FCC ID 2AOKB-A3116. Control on the vendor RFCOMM record 0cf12d31-fac3-4553-bd80-d6832e7b3116 (channel 1 in the capture), whose SDP service name is "CSR GAIA" (the record a Qualcomm/CSR audio SoC reserves for its GAIA control protocol), yet it carries the soundcore 08 ee frames, not GAIA. Frames have NO checksum. Captured firmware 80.01. OpenSCQ30 module: lib/src/devices/soundcore/a3116.rs.

Soundcore Life Q30, over-ear ANC headphones. FCC ID 2AOKB-A3028 (shared with the Life Tune). Control on SPP 00001101-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb according to the vendor app's model table. Frames carry the checksum. Everything about this model is from OpenSCQ30 (lib/src/devices/soundcore/a3028.rs) and SoundcoreManager; nothing was captured.
Soundcore Life Tune, over-ear ANC headphones on the same FCC grant as the Life Q30 (2AOKB-A3028). OpenSCQ30 drives it with the A3028 module unchanged, so every a3028_* command applies. Reported only.

evidence.capture_analysis: Captures were decoded with Wireshark's btrfcomm and btsdp dissectors and a small SDP reassembler for continuation responses. Both logs start with the device already bonded, so no pairing exchange appears. Neither shows GATT traffic to a soundcore service.
open_questions:
The vendor app now requires an account (reviews from 2026-09 describe forced sign-up with v5.0.x) and shows full-screen advertising before its device screen. Nothing on the device side needs either: the control socket is unauthenticated in both captures. This spec is the way around both.
"The app says not connected, but the earbuds play fine" (a recurring review, e.g. Liberty 4 NC in 2023). Audio and control are separate links: A2DP can be up while the RFCOMM control channel is not. Candidate causes on the A3947: another client (or the app's own background service) still holding the control channel, or a client opening the SPP-class record (TOTA, channel 12) instead of the vendor record. Not reproduced.
The Motion+ publishes no SPP-class SDP record. A client that opens "the serial port" by 00001101 finds nothing. OpenSCQ30's A3116 module pins the vendor UUID, and its changelog lists several Motion+ connection fixes; #215 is one such report. Whether this was the cause is not established.
Gaming mode on the Liberty 4 NC "appears enabled but does nothing" (a 2026-09 review). OpenSCQ30 has a model-specific gaming-mode module for the A3947 (builder a3947_gaming_mode). Not examined here.
Why the vendor app sent the A3116 state request twice, 1.3 s apart, at connect: a timeout-and-retry in its connect logic, or a deliberate double read. Harmless either way.

dfu.notes: Recorded only so a client knows it exists and leaves it alone. The A3947 publishes a Bestechnic OTA record ("BESOTA", 66666666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666, RFCOMM channel 13 in the capture; confirmed) and the vendor app bundles a BES updater that opens that UUID (static analysis). No transfer was captured, and no bytes are documented here: an interrupted or wrong image can leave earbuds unbootable, with no known recovery path. Images come from the vendor cloud through the app.

The vendor app has a firmware-update screen for the Motion+ and ships a bundled Qualcomm GAIA BR/EDR service. The Motion+'s control record is named "CSR GAIA", which suggests GAIA is its update path. Neither is verified: the captured record carried soundcore frames, not GAIA, and no update was captured. Some speaker models (Soundcore 3, Mini 3, Motion Boom, Select 2 and others) instead have a per-model OTA UUID in the vendor app: the control UUID with 7c in place of 7b (0cf12d31-fac3-4553-bd80-d6832e7c<sku>). Out of scope; no bytes are documented.

A3028: Open an insecure RFCOMM socket to SPP 00001101-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (from the vendor app's model table).
Send 08 ee 00 00 00 01 01 0a 00 02 (state). That is all OpenSCQ30 sends before normal use.
A3116: Open an insecure RFCOMM socket to 0cf12d31-fac3-4553-bd80-d6832e7b3116 (channel 1 in the capture).
Send 08 ee 00 00 00 01 01 09 00 (state, no checksum); the 45-byte reply arrived in 20 ms. The vendor app sent it a second time 1.3 s later.
The vendor app then sent 01 10 (voice prompt) and 05 01 (undecoded). OpenSCQ30 sends 01 10 only on firmware 38.39 or later.
A3947: Open an insecure RFCOMM socket to 0cf12d31-fac3-4553-bd80-d6832e7b3947 (channel 15 in the capture).
Send 08 ee 00 00 00 01 01 0a 00 02 (state); the 169-byte reply arrived in 50 ms.
The vendor app then sent 08 ee 00 00 00 01 7f 0a 00 80 (LDAC query). No other handshake, no authentication.
connect_sequence.notes: No `initialization` block is declared: there is no handshake to gate the link, and the first request differs by model (with or without a checksum), which a model-independent step list cannot express.

protocol_details.entity_coverage: Not bound to any entity, and why. The EQ curves (a3116_set_custom_eq, a3028_set_equalizer) take eight or nine caller-chosen gains at once and no entity platform holds a curve. a3028_set_equalizer's named presets also need that preset's band values sent along, which lives in OpenSCQ30's preset list rather than in a state field. a3947_request_ldac is a reading with no matching set declared. a3116_request_unknown_0501's reply is not understood. The battery levels are bound raw (0-5) because the device reports steps, not percent.

fast_pair_stream.note: On the A3947 the Android system opened Google's Fast Pair Message Stream (RFCOMM, df21fe2c-2515-4fdb-8886-f12c4d67927c) before the soundcore app connected. It carried group 03 messages: model ID (code 01, D1E4E3, the Liberty 4 NC's Fast Pair model), the device's current BLE address (code 02; the captured value is not reproduced), battery (code 03: left, right and case, one byte each, percent in bits 0-6, bit 7 charging) and, from the phone, platform type (code 08). A client that only wants battery can read it here without the vendor protocol. Format per Google's published specification.

frame_grammar.acknowledgement: The device answers a set with a frame carrying the same two command bytes and an empty payload (length 10 with a checksum, 9 without).
frame_grammar.checksum: sum8 of every preceding byte of the frame, starting with 08/09. Present on the A3947, A3028/A3029 and every OpenSCQ30 model except the A3116, which has none.
frame_grammar.command_bytes: The first command byte groups functions (01 device and general, 02 EQ, 03 EQ with HearID, 04 buttons, 05 A3116 statistics(?), 06 sound modes, 0b multipoint, 10 and 20 hearing-related flags on newer earbuds). The second has its top bit set for a set or change (0x81, 0x83, ...) and clear for a query or report (0x01, 0x03, ...). The meaning of a given pair still varies by model; this is a pattern, not a rule to send by.
frame_grammar.device_to_phone: 09 ff 00 00 01 | cmd[0] cmd[1] | len (u16 LE, whole frame) | payload | [checksum]
frame_grammar.phone_to_device: 08 ee 00 00 00 | cmd[0] cmd[1] | len (u16 LE, whole frame) | payload | [checksum]
frame_grammar.replies: A query's reply carries the same two command bytes as the query.

model_table.description: SKU to control channel, from static analysis of an older vendor Android build (2.9.9, which predates the Liberty 4 NC and the Space range) and normalised here: rows sorted by SKU, UUIDs lower-cased. `control` is `vendor` for 0cf12d31-fac3-4553-bd80-d6832e7b<code>, or `spp` for 00001101-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. `ble_code` is the byte XX of the BLE advertisement code 01XXf5da-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb that build matches (empty where it uses none or something else). `ota_7c` marks models for which it also carries the 7c-sibling OTA UUID. Names are the retail names SoundcoreManager uses. Codes ending in a letter (302b, 339a, 339b, 339c, 392b, 393b, 393c) are regional or hardware revisions of the base SKU and have their own UUID tail. A3947 was added from the capture. A SKU missing from the table is NOT unsupported: the app has gained models since this build, and its vendor UUID follows the same rule (the A3947's did).

remaining_unknowns: The BLE GATT service that SoundcoreManager tunnels frames over: its UUIDs, which models have it (the A3947 and A3116 are not known to), and whether iOS uses it. Deliberately not documented here.
Whether any model requires an application-layer handshake or key before accepting sets. None seen on the A3947 or A3116; newer models (Liberty 5, Space One, Sleep, AeroClip) were not examined.
The meaning of the A3116's 05 01 reply (sixteen u16 values) and of its state byte at offset 12.
The A3947 state bytes OpenSCQ30 marks unknown (offsets 41-45 version string, 68, 117, 142-147, 149, 151, 154-156, 167).
Whether the auto-power-off meaning of the A3116's unsolicited 01 05 push is right; inferred from two echoes.
Whether custom EQ on the A3116 should be selected as preset 0xff (vendor app) or 0x0f (OpenSCQ30), and whether the difference matters to the speaker.
